title: Trump Honors Teen Lifeguard Ryder Williams and Indian-American Boy Nathaniel Rai at White House
excerpt: The president welcomed the 16-year-old California lifeguard and the 10-year-old boy he rescued from powerful surf at Santa Cruz's Seabright Beach last month, calling Williams 'a real hero.'
body:
• President Trump hosted 16-year-old lifeguard Ryder Williams and 10-year-old Indian-American boy Nathaniel Rai at the Oval Office, calling the rescue at Seabright Beach "an amazing thing."
  • Williams rescued Nathaniel from powerful waves at Santa Cruz's Seabright Beach on July 25 after the boy lost consciousness in the water; the rescue was captured on video that went viral.
  • Nathaniel's father, Sumit Rai, who runs Cancer Check Labs screening firefighters for cancer, said Williams' father is a retired firefighter — a coincidence that has deepened the bond between the two families.
  • The Rai family is from Dallas, Texas; Nathaniel is a Jiu-Jitsu champion and martial arts practitioner who was on a California beach vacation when the near-drowning occurred.

A Presidential Welcome

President Donald Trump welcomed California State Lifeguard Ryder Williams and the Indian-American boy he pulled from the ocean last month to the Oval Office on Monday, calling the 16-year-old "a real hero" in a ceremony that brought together two families now bound by a dramatic rescue.

https://x.com/WhiteHouse/status/2089447299533418778

Williams was joined by his parents, Shane and Shannon, while 10-year-old Nathaniel Rai attended with his father Sumit Rai and sister Layla. Aaron Bonin, a fellow lifeguard who assisted in the rescue, was also present, according to NDTV.

"I want to congratulate Nathaniel Rai for coming through an ordeal. That means you are going to have good luck in life," Trump said. Turning to the boy with a grin, he added: "You are very lucky I was not on service that day."

40 Seconds That Changed Everything

The near-drowning occurred on July 25 at Seabright Beach in Santa Cruz, California, during what was supposed to be a relaxing vacation for Nathaniel, his mother Annam, and his 8-year-old sister. Nathaniel was standing in ankle-deep water when a massive wave crashed over him and swept him into dangerous surf.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=R9PHQ2BP_Q0

"I started screaming for help," Nathaniel told Fox News Digital. "I think I saw the lifeguard and then passed out."

Williams, stationed at a tower about 20 yards away, sprinted into the water. He grabbed the boy, who had gone limp and unconscious, and fought to hold on as waves battered them both. Nathaniel weighed about 100 pounds — essentially dead weight in the churning current.

"Two more seconds in the water, he would be thrown another 15, 20 feet out. And at that point, he'd be so far out, you can't see him, let alone rescue or retrieve him. He was in a near-death scenario."

— Sumit Rai, Nathaniel's father

Williams held his position until Bonin reached them to help pull Nathaniel to shore. The boy regained consciousness on the beach and began coughing up sand. Emergency personnel evaluated him and warned about "secondary drowning" — potentially life-threatening complications that can develop hours after a near-drowning event, as reported by Fox News.

A Bond Between Two Families

Sumit Rai was in Dallas when he learned what had happened. The viral video of the rescue — viewed millions of times — added another layer of shock.

"The likelihood of him surviving that incident was infinitesimally small," Sumit told People magazine. "I can never repay him or express enough gratitude."

Since the rescue, the two families have forged an unlikely but deep connection. Sumit said he speaks with Ryder's father Shane daily. The two discovered a shared passion for UFC and mixed martial arts — Nathaniel has trained in MMA since he was 4 and holds gold medals in Gi and No-Gi at the US Open Jiu-Jitsu World League.

The coincidences run deeper. Shane Williams is a retired firefighter. Sumit runs Cancer Check Labs, a nonprofit that screens firefighters for cancer risks associated with their profession — a connection neither family expected, according to Fox News.

"I think of them like an extended family at this point," Sumit said. "Even though I haven't even met them, which is kind of surreal."

From Beach Rescue to National Recognition

The rescue was one of approximately 34 that Santa Cruz County State Parks lifeguards performed over the July 25-27 weekend, driven by hazardous conditions along the coast, according to California State Parks. But Williams' effort stood out — the video captured by a bystander showed the teenager absorbing multiple large waves while refusing to release his grip on the unconscious boy.

"In those dangerous moments, we always try to fall back on our training," Williams said at the White House, according to NDTV. "I really was thinking about how to get the boy out of the water as fast as I can."

The recognition has extended beyond Washington. The cast of Fox's Baywatch reboot, including Shay Mitchell and Stephen Amell, hosted Williams on set, calling him a "real-life superhero," according to People. Williams, whose father was a firefighter, has said he hopes to follow the same career path.

Trump told the visitors they would also be shown President Abraham Lincoln's bedroom, which Lincoln used as his office and Cabinet Room — where he signed the Emancipation Proclamation. For Nathaniel, now back in Dallas and preparing to enter sixth grade, the White House visit capped a summer he will not soon forget.
image_caption: President Trump meets lifeguard Ryder Williams and Nathaniel Rai at the White House. Williams rescued the 10-year-old from dangerous surf at Seabright Beach in Santa Cruz on July 25.
nri_angle: Indian-American boy Nathaniel Rai and his father Sumit Rai were hosted at the White House after Nathaniel's dramatic rescue at a California beach, showcasing an Indian-American family's story on the national stage.
